marking_schemes.question_text: An electrolyte which completely dissociates into ions is: A. Alcohol B. Carbonic acid C. Sucrose D. Sodium hydroxide
marking_schemes.scheme_text: D or Sodium Hydroxide or NaOH
key_points: Strong electrolyte completely dissociates into ions
NaOH is a strong electrolyte
common_errors: Selecting Carbonic acid which is a weak electrolyte
Confusing partial and complete ionisation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: This question was attempted well by majority of the candidates. Some candidates selected Carbonic acid instead of Sodium hydroxide.

marking_schemes.question_text: The most electronegative element from the following elements is: A. Magnesium B. Chlorine C. Aluminium D. Sulphur
key_points: Electronegativity increases across a period
Chlorine has the highest electronegativity among the given elements
common_errors: Choosing Sulphur over Chlorine
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most of the candidates answered this question correctly. A few chose Sulphur over Chlorine.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: The reason for using Aluminium in the alloy duralumin is: A. Aluminium is brittle. B. Aluminium gives strength. C. Aluminium brings lightness. D. Aluminium lowers melting point.
key_points: Aluminium is used in duralumin because of its low density which brings lightness
common_errors: Selecting 'Aluminium is brittle'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates made the error of selecting the option Aluminium is brittle. Most candidates chose the correct option.

marking_schemes.question_text: The drying agent used to dry HCl gas is: A. Conc. H2SO4 B. ZnO C. Al2O3 D. CaO
key_points: Conc. H2SO4 is used to dry acidic gases like HCl
CaO and other basic oxides cannot be used as they react with HCl
common_errors: Selecting CaO which is used for drying ammonia, not HCl
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A few candidates got confused between the drying agent of ammonia and HCl gas and selected CaO instead of conc. H2SO4.

marking_schemes.question_text: A hydrocarbon which is a greenhouse gas is: A. Acetylene B. Ethylene C. Ethane D. Methane
key_points: Methane is a significant greenhouse gas among hydrocarbons
common_errors: Choosing Ethane over Methane
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly, but some chose Ethane over Methane.

marking_schemes.question_text: Conversion of ethanol to ethene by the action of concentrated sulphuric acid is an example of ____________. (dehydration / dehydrogenation / dehydrohalogenation)
key_points: Removal of water from ethanol using conc. H2SO4 is dehydration
Dehydration produces ethene from ethanol
common_errors: Confusing dehydration with dehydrogenation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates were confused between dehydration and dehydrogenation.

marking_schemes.question_text: When sodium chloride is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid below 200°C, one of the products formed is ____________. (sodium hydrogen sulphate / sodium sulphate / chlorine)
key_points: Below 200°C, NaCl + conc. H2SO4 gives NaHSO4 and HCl
Above 200°C, the product would be sodium sulphate
common_errors: Writing Chlorine as the product
Missing the word 'sulphate' from the answer
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates wrote Chlorine instead of Sodium hydrogen Sulphate. Some made errors in writing the correct name by missing out the third word 'sulphate' which was printed on the next line.

marking_schemes.question_text: Ammonia reacts with excess chlorine to form ____________. (nitrogen / nitrogen trichloride / ammonium chloride)
key_points: When chlorine is in excess over ammonia, nitrogen trichloride (NCl3) is formed
When ammonia is in excess, ammonium chloride and nitrogen are formed
common_errors: Selecting ammonium chloride (formed when NH3 is in excess, not Cl2)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number of candidates did not select the correct option.

marking_schemes.question_text: Substitution reactions are characteristic reactions of ____________. (alkynes / alkenes / alkanes)
key_points: Alkanes undergo substitution reactions
Alkenes and alkynes undergo addition reactions due to double/triple bonds
common_errors: Writing alkenes instead of alkanes
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly but some wrote alkenes instead of alkanes.

marking_schemes.question_text: In Period 3, the most metallic element is ____________. (sodium / magnesium / aluminium)
key_points: Metallic character decreases across a period
Sodium is the first element in Period 3 and thus the most metallic among the options
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Almost all candidates attempted this subpart correctly.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for: Reduction of copper (II) oxide by hydrogen.
key_points: CuO is reduced by H2 to form Cu and H2O
Equation must be balanced
common_errors: Writing CuO2 for copper (II) oxide
Writing 2H instead of H2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates wrote the balanced chemical equation correctly. However, a few made the error of writing CuO2 for copper (II) oxide (CuO) and 2H instead of H2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for: Action of dilute sulphuric acid on sodium hydroxide.
key_points: Neutralisation reaction between NaOH and H2SO4
Products are Na2SO4 and H2O
Equation must be balanced with correct coefficients
common_errors: Writing NaSO4 instead of Na2SO4
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote the formula of the product as NaSO4.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for: Action of dilute sulphuric acid on zinc sulphide.
key_points: ZnS reacts with dil. H2SO4 to form ZnSO4 and H2S gas
H2S gas escapes — upward arrow required
common_errors: Representing Zinc sulphide incorrectly as ZnSO3 or ZnSO4
Using HCl instead of H2SO4
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates represented Zinc sulphide incorrectly as ZnSO3 or ZnSO4. Some carelessly used HCl instead of H2SO4.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for: Ammonium hydroxide is added to ferrous sulphate solution.
key_points: FeSO4 reacts with NH4OH to give Fe(OH)2 and (NH4)2SO4
Equation must be balanced
common_errors: Errors in writing formula of ammonium sulphate or ferrous sulphate
Unbalanced equations
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number of candidates made errors in writing the formula of ammonium sulphate or ferrous sulphate. In several cases, the equation was not balanced.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for: Chlorine gas is reacted with ethene.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: H2C=CH2 + Cl2 → H2C(Cl)–CH2(Cl) or C2H4 + Cl2 → C2H4Cl2
key_points: Addition reaction of Cl2 across the double bond of ethene
Product is 1,2-dichloroethane (C2H4Cl2)
common_errors: Writing the product as C2H2Cl2 instead of C2H4Cl2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote the product as C2H2Cl2 instead of C2H4Cl2 in the chemical equation.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one observation for: Concentrated nitric acid is reacted with sulphur.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Reddish brown or brown gas of nitrogen dioxide is formed.
key_points: Reddish brown/brown gas (NO2) is evolved
Must state observation, not write equation or name products only
marking_schemes.model_answer: Reddish brown or brown gas of nitrogen dioxide is formed.
common_errors: Writing the equation instead of observation
Naming products instead of stating observation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates either wrote the equation or named the product formed instead of stating the observation.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one observation for: Ammonia gas is passed over heated copper (II) oxide.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The black copper (II) oxide turns into a pink or reddish-brown substance.
key_points: Black CuO is reduced to pink/reddish-brown copper
Colour change from black to pink/reddish-brown must be stated
marking_schemes.model_answer: The black copper (II) oxide turns into a pink or reddish-brown substance.
accepted_alternatives: Black colour of CuO changes to pink/reddish-brown
common_errors: Describing copper colour as red or reddish or brown without specifying the change from black
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates incorrectly wrote the colour of copper as red or reddish or brown.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one observation for: Copper sulphate solution is electrolysed using copper electrodes.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The colour of the electrolyte remains blue / anode diminishes in size or becomes thinner / cathode becomes thicker.
key_points: Colour of electrolyte remains unchanged (blue)
Anode decreases in mass/size
Cathode increases in mass/size
marking_schemes.model_answer: The colour of the electrolyte remains blue / anode diminishes in size or becomes thinner / cathode becomes thicker.
accepted_alternatives: Anode loses mass; cathode gains mass; blue colour of solution is maintained
common_errors: Stating cathode diminishes in size
Stating blue colour of copper sulphate fades
Noting the change without mentioning the electrode
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: While most candidates answered correctly, some common incorrect responses were: cathode diminishes in size; blue colour of copper sulphate fades. In a few cases, the change was noted without mention of the electrode.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one observation for: A small piece of zinc is added to dilute hydrochloric acid.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Brisk effervescence / A gas given out extinguishes burning splinter and itself burns with pop sound.
key_points: Brisk effervescence observed
Gas produced (H2) burns with a pop sound when a burning splint is brought near
marking_schemes.model_answer: Brisk effervescence is observed. The gas produced extinguishes a burning splint and itself burns with a pop sound.
accepted_alternatives: Bubbles of gas are produced vigorously; gas burns with a squeaky pop
common_errors: Simply identifying the gas as H2 without describing the observation
Stating the gas burns with a blue flame instead of pop sound
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instead of stating the test for the gas evolved, a large number of candidates identified it as H2. Some candidates stated that the gas burns with a blue flame instead of stating that a burning splint is put off with a pop sound.

marking_schemes.question_text: State one observation for: Lead nitrate is heated strongly in a test tube.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: A decrepitating sound is heard / A reddish brown gas is given out / A yellow residue is left behind.
key_points: Decrepitating sound
Reddish brown gas (NO2) evolved
Yellow residue (PbO) left behind
marking_schemes.model_answer: A decrepitating sound is heard / A reddish brown gas is given out / A yellow residue is left behind.
common_errors: Listing products without any noticeable observations
Writing yellow precipitate instead of yellow residue of PbO
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: On heating lead nitrate strongly in a test tube, products formed were listed by many candidates without any noticeable observations. Some candidates wrote yellow precipitate of PbO is obtained instead of yellow residue.

marking_schemes.question_text: Calculate the number of moles in 12g of oxygen gas. [O = 16]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Number of moles in 12g of oxygen gas = 12/32 = 0.375 moles
key_points: Molar mass of O2 = 32 g/mol
Moles = mass / molar mass = 12/32 = 0.375
marking_schemes.model_answer: Molar mass of O2 = 32 g/mol. Moles = 12/32 = 0.375 moles.
common_errors: Taking molar mass of O2 as 16 instead of 32
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates took the mass of one mole of oxygen gas as 16 instead of 32 and hence, could not calculate number of moles correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Calculate the weight of 10^22 atoms of carbon. [C = 12, Avogadro's No. = 6 x 10^23]
key_points: Weight = (number of atoms × atomic mass) / Avogadro's number
common_errors: Incorrect calculation showing inadequate understanding of the concept
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: In a number of cases, calculations for weight of 10^22 atoms of carbon were incorrect indicating inadequate understanding of the concept.

marking_schemes.question_text: Molecular formula of a compound is C6H18O3. Find its empirical formula.
key_points: Divide all subscripts by their HCF
HCF of 6, 18, 3 is 3
C6H18O3 → C2H6O
common_errors: Carrying out elaborate calculations using percentage composition but failing to write the empirical formula
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates attempted well barring some who carried out elaborate calculations using percentage composition but ultimately could not write the empirical formula.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the IUPAC name of the organic compound: H-C(H2)-C≡C-H (i.e., CH3-C≡CH, propyne structure shown)
key_points: Three carbon chain with a triple bond at C1-C2 position
IUPAC name: Propyne
common_errors: Confusion between 'yne' and 'ene'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates attempted this part well. However, some were confused between 'yne' and 'ene'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the IUPAC name of the organic compound: H-C(H2)-C(=O)-H (i.e., CH3-CHO, ethanal structure shown)
key_points: Two carbon chain with an aldehyde functional group
IUPAC name: Ethanal
common_errors: Writing ethanol (alcohol) instead of ethanal (aldehyde)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: In writing IUPAC name of the organic compound, many candidates wrote ethanol (alcohol) which was incorrect.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is the special feature of the structure of ethyne?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Triple bond between 2 carbon atoms / H–C≡C–H
key_points: Ethyne contains a triple covalent bond between the two carbon atoms
marking_schemes.model_answer: Ethyne contains a triple covalent bond between the two carbon atoms (H–C≡C–H).
common_errors: Mentioning linear/planar structure or three covalent bonds rather than specifically a triple covalent bond
Stating it is an unsaturated compound or undergoes addition reaction without specifying triple bond
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates mentioned the presence of a linear planar structure or three covalent bonds rather than presence of triple covalent bond.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the saturated hydrocarbon containing two carbon atoms.
key_points: Saturated hydrocarbon with 2 carbons is ethane (C2H6)
Alkane with 2 carbons
common_errors: Stating ethene or ethyne (which are unsaturated)
Giving the general name of the homologous series instead of the specific compound name
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly while some stated it as ethene or ethyne instead of ethane. A few candidates gave the general name for the homologous series instead of specific name.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the structural formula of Acetic acid.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: H-C(H2)-C(=O)-OH (full structural formula with all bonds shown)
key_points: Must show the full structural formula with all bonds
Carboxyl group (-COOH) attached to methyl group (-CH3)
marking_schemes.model_answer: CH3-C(=O)-OH with all bonds shown explicitly
common_errors: Writing condensed formula of CH3 and COOH instead of structural formula
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates wrote the structural formula of acetic acid correctly. However, some candidates wrote the condensed formula of CH3 and COOH.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the appropriate term: The formula that represents the simplest ratio of the various elements present in one molecule of the compound.
key_points: Empirical formula shows the simplest whole number ratio of atoms in a compound
common_errors: Writing the abbreviation EF instead of the full term
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered this question correctly. Some candidates wrote the abbreviation as EF.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the appropriate term: The substance that releases hydronium ion as the only positive ion when dissolved in water.
key_points: An acid releases H3O+ (hydronium ion) as the only positive ion in water
common_errors: Giving a specific acid name (e.g. hydrochloric acid) instead of the general term 'Acid'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Instead of stating the general term 'Acid' many candidates gave the specific name of an acid which were not acceptable.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the appropriate term: The tendency of an atom to attract electrons towards itself when combined in a covalent compound.
key_points: Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom in a covalent bond to attract the shared electron pair towards itself
common_errors: Writing 'electron affinity' instead of 'electronegativity'
Writing abbreviation form
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates gave the appropriate term as electron affinity instead of electronegativity. Some candidates simply written the abbreviation form of electronegativity.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the appropriate term: The process by which certain ores, specially carbonates, are converted to oxides in the absence of air.
key_points: Calcination converts carbonate ores to oxides in the absence of air
Different from roasting which is done in the presence of air
common_errors: Confusing calcination with roasting
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates mentioned the process correctly. However, a few candidates confused it with roasting.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the appropriate term: The covalent bond in which the electrons are shared equally between the combining atoms.
key_points: When electrons are shared equally, the bond is non-polar covalent
This occurs between identical atoms or atoms with same electronegativity
common_errors: Writing polar covalent bond instead of non-polar covalent bond
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates incorrectly termed it as polar covalent bond.

marking_schemes.question_text: Arrange K, Pb, Ca, Zn in the increasing order of the reactivity.
key_points: Increasing order of reactivity: Pb < Zn < Ca < K
Based on the reactivity series of metals
common_errors: Using > or < symbols instead of arranging in order
Reversing the order
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates used the greater than (>) or less than (<) symbols incorrectly. Some candidates simply arranged the items in reverse order.

marking_schemes.question_text: Arrange Mg2+, Cu2+, Na1+, H1+ in the order of preferential discharge at the cathode.
key_points: Ions lower in the reactivity series are preferentially discharged at cathode
Cu2+ is discharged first, then H+, then Mg2+, then Na+
common_errors: Incorrect ordering
Using symbols incorrectly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates used > or < symbols incorrectly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Arrange Li, K, Na, H in the decreasing order of their ionization potential.
key_points: Ionization potential decreases down a group
H has highest ionization potential among these, then Li, Na, K
common_errors: Reversing the order
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates arranged in reverse order or used symbols incorrectly.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Arrange F, B, N, O in the increasing order of electron affinity.
key_points: N has low electron affinity due to stable half-filled configuration
Increasing order: B < N < O < F
common_errors: Reversing the order
Not accounting for the anomalously low electron affinity of N
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates used > or < symbols incorrectly or arranged in reverse order.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Arrange Ethane, methane, ethene, ethyne in the increasing order of the molecular weight. [H = 1, C = 12]
key_points: Methane (CH4) = 16, Ethyne (C2H2) = 26, Ethene (C2H4) = 28, Ethane (C2H6) = 30
Increasing order: Methane < Ethyne < Ethene < Ethane
common_errors: Using formulae instead of names as given
Incorrect ordering
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates made unnecessary use of formula instead of choosing the names given.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the electron dot structure of: Nitrogen molecule [N = 7]
key_points: Triple bond between two nitrogen atoms shown by three pairs of shared electrons
One lone pair on each nitrogen atom
Total 10 electrons represented (5 from each N)
marking_schemes.model_answer: :N:::N: (triple bond with lone pairs on each nitrogen)
common_errors: Drawing orbit structure instead of electron dot diagram
Forgetting lone pairs on N
Showing electron pairs along with bonds incorrectly
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Candidates drew the orbit structure or showed electron pairs along with the bonds. Some forgot the lone pair of electrons of N.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the electron dot structure of: Sodium chloride [Na = 11, Cl = 17]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Na(circle with dot) + :Cl: → Na+ :Cl:- or Na+Cl-
key_points: Transfer of one electron from Na to Cl shown
Na becomes Na+ and Cl becomes Cl-
Electrons of Na and Cl represented differently (dots and crosses)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Na donates one electron to Cl; Na+ and Cl- ions formed with complete octets shown
common_errors: Not differentiating electrons from Na and Cl
Not showing electron transfer and ion formation
Drawing orbital diagram instead of electron dot diagram
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Electrons of sodium were not differently represented from chlorine; transfer of electron and ion formation was not shown. A few candidates drew the orbital diagram instead of the electron dot diagram.

marking_schemes.question_text: Draw the electron dot structure of: Ammonium ion [N = 7, H = 1]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: [H-N(H)(H)(H)]+ with coordinate bond shown from N to H+
key_points: Coordinate/dative bond from N to H must be shown
Overall 1+ charge on the ion must be shown
Four N-H bonds in tetrahedral arrangement
marking_schemes.model_answer: [H3N→H]+ showing coordinate bond from N to fourth H
common_errors: Not showing coordinate bond
Not showing the overall positive charge on the ion
Drawing ammonia (NH3) instead of ammonium ion (NH4+)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Coordinate bond was not shown by some candidates. Overall positive charge was not shown on the ion in a few cases. Some drew the structure of ammonia instead of ammonium.

marking_schemes.question_text: The pH values of three solutions A (pH=12), B (pH=2), C (pH=7) are given. Which solution will have no effect on litmus solution?
key_points: pH 7 is neutral — no effect on litmus
Solution C has pH 7
common_errors: Attaching specific substance names to solutions instead of using symbols A, B and C
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered the pH value related questions correctly. However, some candidates failed to associate the nature of the substance with the correct pH value.

marking_schemes.question_text: The pH values of three solutions A (pH=12), B (pH=2), C (pH=7) are given. Which solution will liberate CO2 when reacted with sodium carbonate?
key_points: An acid (pH < 7) reacts with sodium carbonate to liberate CO2
Solution B has pH 2, so it is acidic
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates failed to associate the nature of the substance with the correct pH value.

marking_schemes.question_text: The pH values of three solutions A (pH=12), B (pH=2), C (pH=7) are given. Which solution will turn red litmus solution blue?
key_points: A basic/alkaline solution (pH > 7) turns red litmus blue
Solution A has pH 12, so it is alkaline
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates failed to associate the nature of the substance with the correct pH value.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Periodic Table (elements A, B, C, D, E, F, G shown in positions). Which element forms electrovalent compound with G?
key_points: B is a metal that forms an electrovalent (ionic) compound with G (a non-metal)
common_errors: Identifying elements by name instead of using given alphabet letters
Not recognising position of metals and non-metals in the periodic table
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates identified the elements instead of using the given letters of alphabets. In a few cases, the position of metals and non-metals was not clear.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Periodic Table (elements A, B, C, D, E, F, G shown in positions). The ion of which element will migrate towards the cathode during electrolysis?
key_points: Cations (positive ions) migrate towards the cathode
A is a metal that forms a cation
common_errors: Identifying elements instead of using given letters
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Despite the clear instructions not to repeat elements some candidates repeated certain elements.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Periodic Table (elements A, B, C, D, E, F, G shown in positions). Which non-metallic element has the valency of 2?
key_points: E is a non-metal with valency 2 (Group 16 position in the periodic table)
common_errors: Repeating elements already used in earlier sub-parts
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Despite clear instructions not to repeat elements some candidates repeated certain elements.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Periodic Table (elements A, B, C, D, E, F, G shown in positions). Which is an inert gas?
key_points: F is positioned in Group 18 (noble/inert gas group) in the periodic table extract
common_errors: Repeating elements used in earlier sub-parts
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Despite clear instructions not to repeat elements some candidates repeated certain elements.
marking_schemes.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the particles present in: Strong electrolyte
key_points: Strong electrolytes completely dissociate into ions in solution
Only ions are present — no undissociated molecules remain
common_errors: Listing examples of strong electrolytes instead of stating the particles present
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates listed examples instead of stating the presence of ions or molecules depending on the type of electrolyte.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the particles present in: Non-electrolyte
key_points: Non-electrolytes do not ionise in solution
Only molecules are present
common_errors: Listing examples instead of stating particles
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates listed examples instead of stating the presence of ions or molecules.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the particles present in: Weak electrolyte
key_points: Weak electrolytes partially ionise
Both undissociated molecules and ions are present in solution
common_errors: Listing examples instead of stating particles
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates listed examples instead of stating the presence of ions or molecules.

marking_schemes.question_text: Distinguish between Manganese dioxide and copper (II) oxide using concentrated HCl.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: On adding concentrated hydrochloric acid if a greenish yellow gas is evolved it is Manganese dioxide. If no gas is evolved it is CuO.
key_points: MnO2 + conc. HCl → greenish yellow gas (Cl2) evolved
CuO + conc. HCl → no gas evolved; only dissolves to form blue-green solution
marking_schemes.model_answer: On adding concentrated HCl: MnO2 gives a greenish yellow gas (chlorine). CuO produces no gas.
common_errors: Giving equation instead of observation
Specifying result for only one substance and not the other
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some of the candidates gave the equation instead of writing the observation. With the reagent given, the result of adding it to one substance was specified by several candidates but not for the other substance.

marking_schemes.question_text: Distinguish between Ferrous sulphate solution and ferric sulphate solution using sodium hydroxide solution.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: On adding sodium hydroxide solution if a dirty green precipitate is formed it is ferrous sulphate solution. If a reddish-brown precipitate is formed, it is Ferric sulphate solution.
key_points: FeSO4 + NaOH → dirty green precipitate of Fe(OH)2
Fe2(SO4)3 + NaOH → reddish-brown precipitate of Fe(OH)3
marking_schemes.model_answer: On adding NaOH: ferrous sulphate gives a dirty green precipitate; ferric sulphate gives a reddish-brown precipitate.
common_errors: Interchanging the colours of ferrous and ferric precipitates
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates interchanged the colours of the two ions, ferrous and ferric.

marking_schemes.question_text: Distinguish between dilute hydrochloric acid and dilute sulphuric acid using lead nitrate solution.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: On adding lead nitrate solution, if white precipitate is formed which dissolves on heating, then it is dilute HCl. If white precipitate formed does not dissolve on heating, it is dilute H2SO4.
key_points: Both HCl and H2SO4 give white precipitates with lead nitrate
PbCl2 (from HCl) dissolves on heating
PbSO4 (from H2SO4) does not dissolve on heating
marking_schemes.model_answer: Both give white precipitates with Pb(NO3)2, but the precipitate from HCl dissolves on heating while that from H2SO4 does not.
common_errors: Mentioning white precipitate but not the effect of heat on both
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: White precipitate was mentioned by several candidates but the effect of heat on both was not mentioned.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the method of preparation of Lead chloride from: A. Neutralization B. Precipitation C. Direct combination D. Substitution
key_points: Lead chloride is an insoluble salt prepared by precipitation
Mixing soluble lead salt with a chloride solution gives PbCl2 precipitate
common_errors: Incorrectly choosing neutralization
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates incorrectly chose neutralization instead of precipitation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the method of preparation of Iron (II) sulphate from: A. Neutralization B. Precipitation C. Direct combination D. Substitution
key_points: Iron displaces hydrogen from dilute H2SO4 to form FeSO4 — substitution/displacement reaction
Fe + H2SO4 → FeSO4 + H2
common_errors: Writing precipitation instead of substitution
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates erred by writing precipitation instead of substitution.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the method of preparation of Sodium nitrate from: A. Neutralization B. Precipitation C. Direct combination D. Substitution
key_points: Sodium nitrate is a soluble salt prepared by neutralisation of NaOH with HNO3
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: This subpart of the question was attempted correctly by most candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the method of preparation of Iron (III) chloride from: A. Neutralization B. Precipitation C. Direct combination D. Substitution
key_points: Iron (III) chloride is prepared by direct combination of iron and chlorine: 2Fe + 3Cl2 → 2FeCl3
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates attempted this subpart correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following equation: S + conc. HNO3 →
key_points: Sulphur is oxidised to H2SO4 by conc. HNO3
NO2 is the reduction product
Equation must be balanced: S + 6HNO3 → H2SO4 + 6NO2 + 2H2O
common_errors: Writing SO2 as a product instead of H2SO4
Errors in balancing
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: A large number of candidates made errors in balancing of the equation and/or writing the products. Many candidates wrote SO2 as a product instead of H2SO4.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following equation: C + conc. H2SO4 →
key_points: Carbon is oxidised to CO2 by hot conc. H2SO4
H2SO4 is reduced to SO2
Equation must be balanced: C + 2H2SO4 → CO2 + 2SO2 + 2H2O
common_errors: Writing H2CO3 instead of CO2 as product
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Although CO2 was the product, several candidates wrote H2CO3.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the following equation: Cu + dil. HNO3 →
key_points: Dilute HNO3 reacts with Cu to give NO (not NO2)
Products: Cu(NO3)2, NO, H2O
Equation must be balanced: 3Cu + 8HNO3 → 3Cu(NO3)2 + 2NO + 4H2O
common_errors: Writing NO2 as a product instead of NO (NO2 is formed with conc. HNO3)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates wrote NO2 as a product instead of NO.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for the preparation of: Ethene from bromoethane
key_points: Dehydrohalogenation of bromoethane using alcoholic KOH
Bromoethane formula is C2H5Br
Alcoholic KOH condition must be stated
common_errors: Writing bromoethane formula as C2H6Br instead of C2H5Br
Using chloroethane instead of bromoethane
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: The formula for bromoethane was written as C2H6Br in place of C2H5Br by some candidates. Several candidates used chloroethane instead of bromoethane.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for the preparation of: Ethyne using calcium carbide
key_points: Calcium carbide reacts with water to give ethyne and calcium hydroxide
Ca(OH)2 is the correct by-product, not CaO
common_errors: Writing CaO instead of Ca(OH)2 as the product
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: In writing a balanced chemical equation for the preparation of Ethyne using calcium carbide, some candidates wrote the product as CaO instead of Ca(OH)2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Write a balanced chemical equation for the preparation of: Methane from sodium acetate.
key_points: Soda lime decarboxylation of sodium acetate gives methane
Na2CO3 is the by-product
common_errors: Incorrect formula for sodium acetate
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: The formula of sodium acetate was written incorrectly by some candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following organic compound: The compound with 3 carbon atoms whose functional group is a carboxyl.
key_points: 3 carbon atoms + carboxyl group (-COOH) = propanoic acid
IUPAC name: Propanoic acid
common_errors: Drawing the structural formula instead of giving the name
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates incorrectly drew the structural formula when the name of the organic compound was asked.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following organic compound: The first homologue whose general formula is CnH2n.
key_points: CnH2n is the general formula for alkenes
First member (n=2) is ethene (C2H4)
common_errors: Giving answers like alkene, ethyne, or acetylene
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates gave incorrect answers like, alkene, ethyne or acetylene.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following organic compound: The compound that reacts with acetic acid to form ethyl ethanoate.
key_points: Esterification of acetic acid (ethanoic acid) with ethanol gives ethyl ethanoate
The reactant is ethanol
common_errors: Incorrect reactants listed
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: For the compound that reacts with acetic acid to form ethyl ethanoate, reactants listed by many candidates were incorrect.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the following organic compound: The compound formed by complete chlorination of ethyne.
key_points: Complete chlorination of ethyne (C2H2) adds 2Cl2 across the triple bond
Product: CHCl2-CHCl2 = 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane
common_errors: Incorrect numbering of C atoms having the chlorine atoms
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered this subpart correctly. However, some candidates wrote incorrect numbering of the C atoms having the chlorine atoms.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the chemical formula of: Bauxite
key_points: Bauxite is hydrated aluminium oxide
Formula: Al2O3.2H2O
common_errors: Incorrect number of water molecules
Not writing water molecules at all
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: In writing the chemical formula of bauxite, many candidates either wrote incorrect number of water molecules or did not write them at all.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the chemical formula of: Cryolite
key_points: Cryolite is sodium hexafluoroaluminate
Formula: Na3AlF6
common_errors: Writing incorrect formulae
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: In subparts (ii) and (iii), some candidates wrote incorrect formulae.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give the chemical formula of: Sodium aluminate
key_points: Sodium aluminate formula: NaAlO2
common_errors: Writing incorrect formulae
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote incorrect formulae.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is the function of cryolite used along with alumina as the electrolyte in Hall-Heroult's Process?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Cryolite reduces the fusion temperature of the mixture / Cryolite increases the mobility of the ions / increases the conductivity of the electrolyte / Acts as solvent for alumina.
key_points: Cryolite lowers the melting/fusion point of alumina
Increases ionic mobility and conductivity
Acts as solvent for alumina
marking_schemes.model_answer: Cryolite reduces the fusion temperature of the electrolyte mixture and increases its conductivity by acting as a solvent for alumina.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered this question correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is powdered coke sprinkled on top of the electrolyte in Hall-Heroult's Process?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Powdered coke protects the graphite rods of the anode from oxidation by oxygen released at the anode / Powdered coke prevents the loss of heat from the electrolyte.
key_points: Prevents oxidation of graphite anode by O2 released at anode
Prevents heat loss from the electrolyte
marking_schemes.model_answer: Powdered coke is sprinkled to protect the graphite anode from oxidation by oxygen released at the anode and to prevent heat loss from the electrolyte.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered this question correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the electrode from which aluminium is collected in Hall-Heroult's Process.
key_points: Al3+ ions are reduced at the cathode to give aluminium metal
Aluminium is collected at the cathode
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered this question correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Match the alloy Duralumin to its use from: A. Electrical fuse B. Surgical instruments C. Aircraft body D. Decorative articles
key_points: Duralumin is lightweight and strong, used in aircraft body
common_errors: Mismatching alloy uses
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates mismatched Column I and Column II, as they were not sure of the uses of alloys.

marking_schemes.question_text: Match the alloy Solder to its use from: A. Electrical fuse B. Surgical instruments C. Aircraft body D. Decorative articles
key_points: Solder (tin-lead alloy) has a low melting point, used in electrical fuses and soldering
common_errors: Mismatching alloy uses
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates mismatched Column I and Column II.

marking_schemes.question_text: Match the alloy Brass to its use from: A. Electrical fuse B. Surgical instruments C. Aircraft body D. Decorative articles
key_points: Brass (copper-zinc alloy) is used for decorative articles
common_errors: Mismatching alloy uses
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates mismatched Column I and Column II.

marking_schemes.question_text: Match the alloy Stainless Steel to its use from: A. Electrical fuse B. Surgical instruments C. Aircraft body D. Decorative articles
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Stainless Steel: B or Surgical instruments
key_points: Stainless steel (iron-chromium-nickel alloy) is corrosion resistant, used in surgical instruments
common_errors: Mismatching alloy uses
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates mismatched Column I and Column II.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify the substance: The catalyst used to oxidise ammonia.
key_points: Platinum is the catalyst used in the oxidation of ammonia in Ostwald's process
common_errors: Mentioning Fe, V2O5, or CaO as the catalyst
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates identified the catalyst used to oxidise ammonia correctly. However, a few candidates mentioned incorrect catalyst such as Fe/V2O5/CaO.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify the substance: The organic compound which when solidified, forms an ice like mass.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Acetic acid or ethanoic acid or CH3COOH
key_points: Glacial acetic acid is pure acetic acid which solidifies to an ice-like mass at around 16.7°C
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Almost all candidates answered correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Identify the substance: The dilute acid which is an oxidizing agent.
key_points: Dilute nitric acid acts as an oxidising agent
HCl and H2SO4 do not act as oxidising agents in dilute form
common_errors: Writing HCl or H2SO4 as the oxidising acid
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates listed HCl or H2SO4 as an oxidising agent instead of nitric acid.

marking_schemes.question_text: 2NaOH + CuSO4 → Na2SO4 + Cu(OH)2↓. What mass of copper hydroxide is precipitated by using 200g of sodium hydroxide? [H=1, O=16, Na=23, S=32, Cu=64]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: RMW of NaOH = 40, Cu(OH)2 = 98. 2 x 40g NaOH precipitates 98g Cu(OH)2. 200g NaOH precipitates = (98 × 200) / 80 = 245g
key_points: Molar mass NaOH = 40
Molar mass Cu(OH)2 = 98
2 mol NaOH → 1 mol Cu(OH)2
200g NaOH = 5 mol NaOH → 2.5 mol Cu(OH)2 = 245g
common_errors: Using Gay Lussac's law instead of mole concept
Incorrect molecular mass calculation
Not accounting for the stoichiometric coefficient of 2 for NaOH
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates used Gay Lussac's law instead of mole concept or calculated the molecular mass incorrectly. Some candidates failed to use the stoichiometric coefficients i.e. 2 in the case of NaOH.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is the colour of the precipitate of copper hydroxide formed?
key_points: Cu(OH)2 precipitate is pale blue in colour
common_errors: Writing brown or white as the colour of the precipitate
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates incorrectly wrote the colour of the precipitate as brown or white.

marking_schemes.question_text: Find the empirical formula and the molecular formula of an organic compound from the data given below: C = 75.92%, H = 6.32% and N = 17.76%. The vapour density of the compound is 39.5. [C = 12, H = 1, N = 14]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Empirical formula: C5H5N. Empirical formula weight = 79. n = (2 × 39.5) / 79 = 1. Molecular formula = C5H5N.
key_points: Divide by smallest (1.267): C = 5, H = 5, N = 1
Empirical formula = C5H5N
Molecular mass = 2 × VD = 2 × 39.5 = 79
Molecular formula = C5H5N
marking_schemes.model_answer: Empirical formula: C5H5N. Molecular formula: C5H5N.
common_errors: Determining empirical formula correctly but failing to calculate n and hence erring in molecular formula
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates determined the empirical formula correctly but failed in calculating the value of n and hence, erred in the molecular formula.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the gas evolved in: Alumina undergoes electrolytic reduction.
key_points: During electrolytic reduction of alumina, oxygen is evolved at the anode
Aluminium is deposited at the cathode
common_errors: Writing CO2 instead of O2
Writing nascent oxygen [O]
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Some candidates wrote the name of the gas evolved on electrolytic reduction of alumina as CO2 instead of O2. A few candidates wrote the symbol of nascent oxygen, that was not acceptable.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the gas evolved in: Ethene undergoes hydrogenation reaction.
key_points: Hydrogenation of ethene adds H2 across the double bond to give ethane
C2H4 + H2 → C2H6
common_errors: Writing H2 is evolved — H2 is a reactant in hydrogenation, not a product
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Several candidates wrote H2 is evolved in the hydrogenation reaction of ethene, which was an incorrect answer.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the gas evolved in: Ammonia reacts with heated copper oxide.
key_points: Ammonia reduces heated CuO: 2NH3 + 3CuO → N2 + 3Cu + 3H2O
Nitrogen gas is evolved
common_errors: Writing N, NO, or NO2 instead of N2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: In the reaction of ammonia with heated copper oxide, the gas evolved was incorrectly written as N, NO or NO2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the flow chart: Mg3N2 →[A]→ NH3. Give balanced equation to represent reaction A.
key_points: Metal nitride reacts with water to give metal hydroxide and ammonia
Mg3N2 + 6H2O → 3Mg(OH)2 + 2NH3
common_errors: Writing MgO instead of Mg(OH)2 as the product
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: For reaction A, MgO was written as the product instead of Mg(OH)2.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the flow chart: NH3 →[B]→ NH4Cl. Give balanced equation to represent reaction B.
key_points: NH3 reacts with HCl to form NH4Cl
Alternatively, with excess NH3 and Cl2: 8NH3 + 3Cl2 → 6NH4Cl + N2
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates gave correct balanced equations to represent reactions A, B and C.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the flow chart: NH4Cl →[C]→ NH3. Give balanced equation to represent reaction C.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: NH4Cl + NaOH → NaCl + NH3 + H2O Or with any other alkali.
key_points: Ammonium salt reacts with an alkali (e.g. NaOH) to release NH3
NH4Cl + NaOH → NaCl + NH3 + H2O
common_errors: Failing to use an alkali in reaction C
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: For reaction C, some candidates failed to use an alkali.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the table for industrial preparation of Ammonia: Name of the process
key_points: Ammonia is industrially manufactured by Haber's Process
common_errors: Writing Ostwald's process or Baeyer's process
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Name of the process was incorrectly written as Ostwald's process/Baeyer's process.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the table for industrial preparation of Ammonia: Catalytic equation (with the catalyst)
key_points: N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3 with iron (Fe) as catalyst
Iron catalyst must be mentioned
common_errors: Writing platinum or nickel as catalyst instead of iron
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: The catalyst listed was platinum/nickel, etc. instead of iron.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the table for industrial preparation of Sulphuric acid: Name of the process
key_points: Sulphuric acid is industrially manufactured by Contact Process
common_errors: Writing Haber's Process instead of Contact Process
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Haber's Process was written instead of Contact Process.

marking_schemes.question_text: Complete the table for industrial preparation of Sulphuric acid: Catalytic equation (with the catalyst)
key_points: 2SO2 + O2 → 2SO3 with V2O5 (vanadium pentoxide) or Pt as catalyst
Key step in Contact Process
common_errors: Incorrect equation or incorrect catalyst
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Incorrect equation was given by some candidates.
